Three public-dataset runs had 3.7–4.2 cm trajectory error; under-voltage prevents a speed verdict.
The 8-gigabyte (GB) Pi boots. Power, sustained storage and this camera’s calibration remain
unresolved.
STM32H7 retains balance and motor safety throughout the roadmap.

2/22

P0: prepare tools and bookings before using the camera.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Can the next lab slot produce useful evidence?
Audit receipts; test a tiny synthetic import; prepare the target, stationary recorder
and interface proposal.
Existing Python fixtures, hash bundles, Kalibr import pilot and source inspection.
Mac now; confirm lab workstation, target, cooler, data storage and controller board.
Tooling preserves pixels, counts and timestamps; command cards, approvals and lab
dependencies are ready.
2–5 engineer-days. You confirm deliveries, loan duration, overnight permission and
controller owner.
No camera or SLAM execution until you explicitly say CAMERA AVAILABLE.
3/22

P1: fresh sensor and ROS gates establish trustworthy input.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Do power, transport, recording and replay hold together?
Platform review, then N1 → N2 → N3; stop and diagnose the first unmet condition.
Guarded native tools; librealsense; Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) Jazzy and bag
replay.
8 GB Pi, suitable supply/cooling, current camera, direct Universal Serial Bus (USB) 3
cable and qualified storage.
Camera branch ≥5000M; exact raw stages and complete isolated ROS replay pass
actual review.
0.5–3 engineer-days; request a 3–4 h bench slot. You secure power, access and the
current unit.
N2 keeps its 20, 105 and mandatory 300-second stages; a short demo cannot replace them.
4/22

P2: capture geometry, timing and noise on the same unit.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Can this camera’s calibration be identified and checked?
Audit the first target take, then three all-axis motion takes and held-out room motion;
record stationary inertial data separately.
Reviewed recorder/converter, tag detector and per-stream count/time audit.
Measured A0 AprilGrid, rigid backing/stand, usable infrared light, Pi power/cooling
and qualified data medium.
Target and motion coverage are usable; original data and warnings have two verified
copies; noise fits have sufficient support.
1–2 engineer-days plus 15–24 h stationary recording. You book 3–4 h target work and
overnight access.
The current 120-second stereo recorder needs a separate reviewed tool for overnight inertial data.
5/22

P3: replay with trusted calibration separates the faults.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Do fixed trusted inputs give repeatable tracking?
Finish the interrupted rebuild; check linkage; rerun the public reference, solve
camera–inertial calibration and repeat held-out replay.
Existing ORB-SLAM3, Kalibr, Allan noise analysis and trajectory evaluation.
Powered Pi for rebuild/replay; Mac or tested lab workstation for calibration.
Parameters and transforms are traceable; initialization, tracking and reset histories
satisfy reviewed bounds across retained repeats.
2–4 engineer-days; tool incompatibility can add 2–5 days. You review calibration and
arrange recapture if needed.
A plausible room path cannot establish accuracy without an appropriate reference.
6/22

P4: live estimates must remain fresh under sustained load.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Does useful output arrive before it becomes stale?
Use the same binary/settings; three short live repeats, then sustained load with loops,
map growth and recovery.
Native headless estimator; source-age, queue, input-loss, central processing unit
(CPU), memory and power observers.
Final Pi/camera/cables/cooling/storage; textured marked room route.
No unexplained loss or growing backlog; age tails and resources meet agreed
bounds, with honest loss/reset state.
1–3 engineer-days; book 2–3 h after replay review. You agree limits with the
controller owner before acceptance.
A fresh heartbeat does not make an old camera estimate fresh.
7/22

P5: review health semantics and prove rejection offline.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Can STM32 reject believable but unusable estimates?
Review session, sequence, frame, source age and validity; exercise stale, corrupt,
reset and frozen-pose fixtures.
Future modular health adapter, bounded receiver/parser, clock mapper and
synthetic fault harness.
Development host and confirmed controller board/pinout; reuse a proven link, else
propose dedicated 3.3 V serial.
Every fixture yields the expected rejection or fallback; invalid input never renews
motion authority.
2–4 engineer-days, parallel with calibration/live work. You approve the interface and
name its controller implementer.
Health-only comes first; the new message and firmware remain proposals until reviewed.
8/22

P6: supported robot tests expose power and control coupling.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Does mounted perception disturb local control?
Qualify the battery rail and rigid torso mount; refresh relevant input checks; begin
with motors-disabled health and injected faults.
Approved sender/receiver, supply and controller-loop traces, age/counter logs.
Actual robot, body sensor, reviewed power/link/mount, cooling, debugger, rated
stand and independent stop.
No unexpected actuation/reset or loop-limit breach; each fault withdraws optional
input within approved bounds.
1–3 engineer-days; book 3–4 h with the controller owner. You approve electrical,
mount and supported-test plans.
A stand proves bench behavior; free balance still needs its own test.
9/22

P7: repeat slow supervised motion, then freeze the deployment.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Can the robot repeat the result and handle Pi loss?
Independent controller baseline; tethered balance first, then bounded manual room
driving with advisory localization; test faults and reproduce handoff.
Same reviewed stack, controller traces, route checks, frozen runtime bundle and
operator runbook.
Approved restraint/clear room, local stop, controller owner, operator/spotter and
final hardware.
Retained repeats meet tracking, age, loop and fallback bounds; another operator
reproduces startup, stop and rollback.
1–4 engineer-days; reserve 2–3 h motion plus a repeat slot. You approve motion
limits and review every trial.
The first deployment is advisory localization during supervised slow indoor motion.
10/22

P8: navigation needs continuous odometry and obstacle coverage.
Question How Tools Hardware Done when Time / you Can it reach goals with clearance and local controller veto?
Validate wheel/body telemetry and clocks; qualify continuous odometry, depth/map
input and command limits; repeat staged goal/fault tests.
Reviewed ROS adapter, justified local filter, Nav2 and optional Real-Time
Appearance-Based Mapping (RTAB-Map).
Deployed robot, qualified obstacle coverage, surveyed room, local stop and
controller owner.
Repeated goals meet agreed position/heading/clearance bounds; every
stale/reset/loss event cancels navigation safely.
Additional 2–4+ weeks, low confidence. You approve this scope, graph, fusion and
command interface separately.
ORB’s sparse landmarks alone do not provide an obstacle map.

13/22

STM32 validates optional input and keeps local balance authority.

age, frame, validity
Pi

Accepted sequence, fault and controller status
Stale, absent, invalid or reset input: revoke optional navigation.
STM32 performs approved bounded stopping.
Local balance and motor protections remain active.
IMU means inertial measurement unit. Physical link, age limits and fallback timing need controller review.
14/22

Keep one default estimator and switch only on matched evidence.
Both reviews favor ORB next. The independent review challenges that choice when the deliverable changes. Its
scores are planning judgments, not Pi benchmarks.
Candidate /100 Why choose it / what is missing
ORB stereo-inertial RTAB-Map own odometry OpenVINS local VIO Wheel/body + depth 68 68 61 56 Existing build/input path; calibrated live behavior still open.
Mapping-first alternative; complete Pi load still unmeasured.
Freshness challenger; Pi/Jazzy build and global mapping need
work.
Earlier rolling demo if existing controller exports are proven.
Keep ORB for localization now. Prefer RTAB for a mapping-first goal if measured workload passes;
compare OpenVINS on identical data if ORB misses reviewed bounds.
VIO means visual-inertial odometry. Changing the objective can change the best first demo.
15/22

Global corrections must not jump the local motion state.
Robot body
Reviewed mount
Global map

Local odometry
Must stay continuous
SLAM alignment Local estimator
Camera pose must be transformed into a clearly named robot frame at the correct source epoch.
Loop closure and reset change global alignment; they cannot become a balance-state jump.
Before fusion, validate wheel contact/slip, body-sensor clocks and measurement lineage.
16/22

Stop at the failing layer before changing algorithms or scope.
Early warning Next action
Power faults or storage gaps Qualify the supply/data medium under the real load; repeat relevant
Poor target/import/noise support Age grows or tracking repeatedly
fails

disturbance
No independent room reference gates.
Inspect the pilot, repair tools or recapture while the unit is available.
Correct calibration/timing; profile one variable; compare one
alternative on matched data.
Receiver rejects old source epochs and revokes optional input.
Return to supported tests; review mount, wiring and controller
limits.
Report continuity/checkpoint proxies with uncertainty; accuracy
stays open.
17/22

Decide the boundaries before consuming the robot slot.
Storage: retain the approved calibration-card exception; borrow qualified external storage when
gate tooling needs it.
Software: native estimator plus reviewed health adapter first; add ROS SLAM integration for a real
consumer.
Link: reuse a proven controller link; otherwise review dedicated 3.3 V serial before implementation.
Acceptance: agree source age, loop limits, stopping and motion envelope from measured
evidence.
Scope: advisory deployment first; approve navigation, message/graph changes and motion
separately.
18/22

This week, secure the inputs and finish camera-free preparation.
14–20 October 2026
You: confirm supply/card arrival, camera loan, cooler/storage/console and the controller
board/person.
You: request the fresh-gate slot, target slot and overnight access; provisionally hold the robot week.
Engineer: prepare reader/recorder fixtures, measured target and reviewable health/clock proposal.
At the bench: explicit camera authorization and stable power precede fresh N1, N2 and N3.
Week’s exit: reviewed entry evidence or a precise blocker, plus tools ready for calibration capture.
19/22

Next week, capture once, inspect early and protect the raw data.
Week of 21 October 2026
You: bring the same unit and measured A0 target; confirm lighting, metrology, backup space and
overnight permission.
Engineer: audit the first target take before repeating; retain three calibration takes and held-out
room motion.
Together: start the tested stationary recorder, verify normal stop and make two checksum-verified
copies.
In parallel: analyze calibration and prepare reviewed receiver fixtures, mount and battery rail.
If fresh gates or tools are incomplete, carry that work forward; preserve the overnight and soak
requirements.
20/22

Use each later week to answer one deployment question.
Target week Question and exit
28 Oct–3 Nov 4–10 Nov 11–17 Nov 18–24 Nov Does calibrated replay carry into fresh live output? Accept age/resource
evidence and receiver fixtures.
Does the mounted stack preserve controller authority? Retain supported-robot
power, loop and fault traces.
Does slow supervised motion repeat and survive Pi loss? Review retained trials
and reproducible handoff.
Which failing layer needs repair/recapture? Hold a repeat slot and freeze only
evidenced behavior.
Parts, tools, controller readiness and bookings can shift these targets. Navigation begins after a
separate scope decision.
21/22

The recommendations trace to project facts and primary sources.
Project evidence: 13–14 October session facts, current lab runbook, known-dataset report,
architecture decisions and calibration plan.
ORB-SLAM3 and OpenVINS: estimator capabilities and licences; OpenVINS Jazzy proposal.
Kalibr calibration, transform/time conventions and stationary noise guidance.
Raspberry Pi hardware guidance: supply, peripheral power and cooling.
ROS frame conventions, Nav2 odometry requirements and RTAB-Map ROS 2 backend.
Durations and switch policies are planning judgments. Hardware stock, acceptance bounds and
deployed performance need confirmation.
22/22
